annotations.title: Set a model key's gateway, supply, price, speed or input:output ratio

description:
Set a model key's gateway, supply, price, speed or input:output ratio

Changes one of the account's own model keys: `gateway` sets or clears the gateway it runs through by default (a gateway's name from the `list_gateways` tool, or null for none; requests on the key then go through it, and a request naming another with the x-klinn-gateway header is refused with 403 gateway_locked), `communitySupply` sets whether community-supplied capacity may serve its requests (false keeps every request on our own routes), and `maxPrice` sets or clears its default limit order ({input, output, cache} USD per 1M tokens; prompt, completion and input_cache_read are accepted too: a request nothing in the market is within is refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit and billed nothing). `minDiscount` sets or clears its default minimum discount (0 to 100: its requests are served only at least that many percent under a model's list price; the same 422 when nothing in the market is). `speed` sets or clears its default speed ({sort, minThroughput, maxLatencySecs}: a request's own settings and its gateway's come first; see /docs/speed). `priceFallover` sets whether its requests may go to a dearer source when none can serve them at the model's price (false keeps them at the model's price, null returns to the default, on; see /docs/errors#fallover). `ioRatio` sets or clears its expected input:output ratio (a number such as 15, or a string such as "15:1" or "1:4": routes are ranked at the prompt divided by it instead of at max_tokens; a request's own x-klinn-io-ratio header and its gateway's io_ratio come first; see /docs/speed#io-ratio). Each field changes only when given; give at least one. New requests follow within about a minute. A name no gateway of yours has is 400 invalid_request; a revoked key, a customer's key or an unknown id is 404. Returns the key.

communitySupply.description: Whether community-supplied capacity may serve the key's requests; false keeps every request on our own routes. New requests follow within about a minute.

gateway.description: The name of the gateway the key's requests run through by default (one of GET /gateways), or null for none.

ioRatio.description: The key's expected input:output ratio, as a number of input tokens per output token (15) or a string such as "15:1" or "1:4"; null clears it. A request's own x-klinn-io-ratio header and its gateway's io_ratio come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

maxPrice.description: The key's default limit order: the most its requests are billed per 1M tokens, per leg; null clears it. A request's own limit and its gateway's come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

oneOf.description: A limit order's maximum price: the most a request is billed per 1M tokens, on the input leg, the output leg, the cache leg or several (at least one), each compared on its own. Send {"input", "output", "cache"}; the compatible names prompt, completion and input_cache_read (also cache_read) are the same legs and are accepted too, but a leg given under two names with different values is a 400. It is stored and returned under the compatible names (prompt, completion, input_cache_read). A request nothing in the market is within is refused with 422 no_offer_under_limit and billed nothing; a request with no limit is matched at the market price.

cache.description: USD per 1M input tokens read from the cache. A route that bills cached tokens at its input price is compared at that price.

cache_read.description: Another name for cache, accepted on input.

completion.description: The compatible name for output; returned under this name.

input_cache_read.description: The compatible name for cache; returned under this name.

prompt.description: The compatible name for input; returned under this name.

minDiscount.description: The key's default minimum discount, 0 to 100: its requests are served only at least this many percent under a model's list price; null clears it. A request's own and its gateway's can only make it stricter. New requests follow within about a minute.

priceFallover.description: Whether the key's requests may go to a dearer source when none can serve them at the model's price: false keeps them at the model's price, true allows it, null returns to the default (on). The request's own allow_price_fallover setting, and any price limit, come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

speed.description: The key's default speed ({sort, minThroughput, maxLatencySecs}); null clears it. A request's own settings and its gateway's come first. New requests follow within about a minute.

oneOf.description: How requests pick among the routes that can serve a model. `sort` orders the routes: `price` (cheapest first, the default), `throughput` (fastest tokens per second first; the :nitro suffix) or `latency` (quickest to the first token first). `minThroughput` and `maxLatencySecs` are best effort: routes that meet them come first, and when none does the request is still served by the next best route. A request that sets allow_fallbacks to false makes them strict instead (503 no_route_meets_speed). Community-supplied routes must also reach at least half the model's median speed to get traffic. Balanced is {sort: price, minThroughput: 30}; Fastest is {sort: throughput}. max_price still caps the price.

maxLatencySecs.description: Seconds to the first token a route should stay within; null for no ceiling.

minThroughput.description: Tokens per second a route should reach; null for no floor.

sort.description: What the routes are ordered by.
